newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Zhenhai plunges 10 pct on oil price hike.
newsitem.headline: Zhenhai plunges 10 pct on oil price hike.

text.p: Shares of China's Zhenhai Refining & Chemical Co Ltd plunged nearly 10 percent Tuesday afternoon on fears that the U.S. attacks on targets in Iraq would trigger higher oil prices, analysts said.
Zhenhai fell 22.5 cents, or 9.9 percent to a low of HK$2.05 before recovering slightly to close at HK$2.075, down 20 cents.
Analysts said oil prices were rising and Zhenhai was the first H share to be hit.
"Zhenhai is most vulnerable and the others receive more subsidies from the state," said Elizabeth Cheng at HSBC James Capel Asia Ltd.
SIMEX Brent futures for October touched a high of US$23.50 in the afternoon, versus a previous high of US$22.68 in mid-April.
Zhenhai, which relies heavily on imported oil, was rated the third largest oil refiner in the country with a primary refining capacity of eight million tonnes per year.
The company earlier estimated that domestic crude oil would only account for 17 percent of its overall processing throughput in 1996.
